samples.summary: The CI-fix loop's `Summarize the failure` step runs the deleted `./scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs`, and it is not continue-on-error — the `iterate` job now fails before the fixer is ever dispatched.
samples.evidence: `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:306` runs `DIAG="$(node ./scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs)"`. That path resolves against THIS repo's checkout (line 106, `actions/checkout@v4` of the head branch); the pinned pipeline is staged to `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools` at line 147 and `.trusted-agent` is deleted at line 149, so `scripts/agent/` is never replaced by the adapter in this job. This diff deletes `scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs` (the only remaining copy in the tree is `.trusted/`, a checkout artifact), and it is not in `FILES`/`ASSETS` in `scripts/vendor-pipeline.mjs`, so it is not vendored either. The step (lines 299-312) carries no `continue-on-error`, so it reds the `iterate` job, and every later step is gated on `steps.guard.outputs.proceed == 'true'` — `Run Claude Code` at line 334 never runs. Compare the sibling steps at lines 271 and 470, which correctly use `"$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools/loop-status.mjs"`. Fix belongs on line 306: point it at `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools/summarize-ci.mjs` (with the same `[ -f … ] || exit 0` guard the loop-status steps use).

samples.summary: Five more steps in the same `iterate` job invoke `./scripts/agent/{set-state,metrics}.mjs` from the deleted mirror; all are continue-on-error, so the CI-fix loop silently stops labelling state and recording effort.
samples.evidence: All resolve against this repo's checkout (line 106), not the adapter: `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:247` (`metrics.mjs summarize`), `:257` (`set-state.mjs "$PR" blocked`), `:332` (`set-state.mjs "$PR" fixing`), `:454` (`set-state.mjs "$PR" blocked || true`), `:491` (`metrics.mjs record --kind ci-fix`). `set-state.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` are both gone from `scripts/agent/` after this diff — `set-state.mjs` moved to `scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/set-state.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` was already vendored there. Lines 253/328/487 are `continue-on-error: true` and line 454 ends in `|| true`, so each fails invisibly: a paged PR never gets `agent:blocked`, an in-flight round never gets `agent:fixing`, and no `ci-fix` session is written to the metrics ledger. The diff already applied exactly this fix in `agent-implement.yml` (lines 285/362/376 → `./scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/…`) but did not carry it to this workflow.

samples.summary: `harvest.mjs` still reads `scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json`, which this diff moves to vendor; the loader swallows the failure and returns `[]`, so `panelSaw` is empty for every PR and every human fix is recorded as a panel MISS.
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:66` — `const LENSES_PATH = path.join(HERE, "lenses", "lenses.json")`. The diff renames `scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json` to `scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/lenses/lenses.json`, and this line was not updated (there is no `--lenses` flag to override it). `loadLensNames()` at `scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:2042-2049` catches the read failure, logs `"panelSaw will be empty"` to stderr and returns `[]`; `cmdHarvest` consumes it at `scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:2119`. An empty name list makes `latestLensRuns(runs, [])` (imported from `./vendor/pipeline/prior-findings.mjs` / `review-state.mjs`) match nothing, so no panel rounds are found, `panelSawAt` (`harvest.mjs:1751`) returns `{reviewedSha:"", conclusion:"", blockingFindings:0}`, and the comparison set is empty — every candidate becomes an unmatched `miss` record. The command still exits 0 with only a stderr line, so nothing surfaces the corruption. Fix on line 66: `path.join(HERE, "vendor", "pipeline", "lenses", "lenses.json")`.

samples.summary: `DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT` still names the deleted `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs`, while the same diff updated the sibling test's `REAL_PANEL` and this file's `lensesDir` default to vendor — a default replay spawns a missing script, and no replay can record a measured `panel_sha` any more.
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:81` — `export const DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT = path.join(HERE, "..", "review-panel.mjs")`, i.e. `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs`, deleted by this diff. It is used at `scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:754` (`panelScript: path.resolve(args["panel-script"] ?? DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT)`) and passed to `reviewerAdapter` at `:861`; the adapter refuses a non-existent panel (`scripts/agent/eval/adapters/reviewer.test.mjs:231`). Second, worse consequence: `resolvePanelSha` (`scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:528`) THROWS for any `--panel-script` that is not `DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT`, so passing the vendored panel is refused and demands a hand-supplied `--panel-sha`; on the default path it reads `git rev-parse HEAD` of `path.dirname(panelScript)` = `scripts/agent` (`:534-537`), stamping this repo's HEAD as the reviewer's identity for a directory that no longer contains the panel. `run.test.mjs:447` asserts `o.panelScript === path.resolve(DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT)`, which is tautological and passes either way, so CI cannot catch it. The diff already updated `scripts/agent/eval/adapters/reviewer.test.mjs:37` `REAL_PANEL` to `vendor/pipeline/review-panel.mjs` and `run.mjs:752` `lensesDir` to vendor — line 81 is the one that was missed.

samples.summary: `cache-report.mjs`'s default `--lenses-dir` still points at the moved `scripts/agent/lenses`; only its test was updated to pass the vendor path, so the default invocation is broken and untested.
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/cache-report.mjs:248` — `loadLenses(path.resolve(String(args["lenses-dir"] ?? path.join(HERE, "lenses"))))`. `scripts/agent/lenses/` is renamed to `scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/lenses/` by this diff, so `node scripts/agent/cache-report.mjs` with no flag now throws in `loadLenses` (which does an unguarded `readFileSync(path.join(dir, "lenses.json"))`, `vendor/pipeline/review-panel.mjs:2365`). The diff changed `scripts/agent/cache-report.test.mjs:138` to `loadLenses(path.join(HERE, "vendor", "pipeline", "lenses"))` — passing the directory explicitly — which is precisely why the broken default is invisible to the suite. The usage banner at `scripts/agent/cache-report.mjs:18` also still advertises the old default. Fix on line 248: default to `path.join(HERE, "vendor", "pipeline", "lenses")`.

samples.summary: The panel's `fix` job runs `./scripts/agent/set-state.mjs` twice AFTER the branch checkout, deliberately using the branch's own copy — which no branch has once this merges, so the `agent:fixing` label and the paged `agent:blocked` label stop being set.
samples.evidence: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1647` (`Set state → fixing`) and `:1897` (`node ./scripts/agent/set-state.mjs "$PR" blocked || true`) both run after the PR-branch `actions/checkout@v4` at `:1621`, which replaces the workspace and therefore the adapter's pipeline copy placed at `scripts/agent` on line 1471. The comment at `:1638-1640` states this on purpose ("Uses the branch's own checkout"). Post-merge every branch has `scripts/agent/vendor/pipeline/set-state.mjs` and no `scripts/agent/set-state.mjs`, so both invocations fail — silently, since line 1643 is `continue-on-error: true` and line 1897 ends in `|| true`. Effect is advisory-only label drift (the lifecycle label is a projection, not a gate), but it is a reachable break the diff did not update. Either repoint at `vendor/pipeline/set-state.mjs` or use the already-staged `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools/set-state.mjs` (staged at `:1601`).

samples.summary: The new drift guard inspects only ES import specifiers, so filesystem references to moved pipeline files (`path.join`, spawned script paths) and workflow `run:` invocations are entirely outside its coverage — which is how the five breakages above passed it.
samples.evidence: `scripts/verify-pipeline-drift.mjs:142` — `mirrorImports` matches only `IMPORT_RE` (`:36`, `from`/`import`/`import()` specifiers) and resolves those. It never reads a `path.join(...)` argument, so `scripts/agent/harvest.mjs:66` (`path.join(HERE, "lenses", "lenses.json")`) and `scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:81` (`path.join(HERE, "..", "review-panel.mjs")`, later spawned) are invisible to it. It also scans only `scripts/agent`, so no `.github/workflows/**` `run:` line is checked — `agent-iterate-ci.yml:306` and the four sibling invocations are outside its root. The header claims this check converts "a runtime crash inside a hunt or a replay" into a CI failure on the causing commit; for the two largest remaining reference classes it does not. A cheap complement would be to also flag string literals under `scripts/agent/` that name a `pipelineFiles` member, and to scan `.github/workflows/*.yml` for `scripts/agent/<pipeline-file>` outside an adapter'd job.
searchedFor: read scripts/verify-pipeline-drift.mjs lines 28-175 (IMPORT_RE, STAYS, walk, reappearedMirrorFiles, mirrorImports, main)
scripts/test/verify-pipeline-drift.test.mjs for any workflow- or literal-path assertion
